findings.reason: The protected source is a clear optimal pivot-and-distance-frequency solution. Squared-distance arithmetic, incremental ordered-pair counting, and per-pivot map reset are expressed directly with precise coordinate and frequency names; no inert candidate would materially improve it.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 447 and its Python point-array-to-count surface. The app solve signature and native numberOfBoomerangs method accept the same distinct two-dimensional coordinates and return the same ordered-tuple count. The modular Reference preserves the pivot semantics and all five source constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064839163. The app and native implementations iterate the same pivots and points, compute the identical squared distance, read and increment the same per-pivot frequency, add twice the prior count, and return the same accumulator; only annotations and the Solution wrapper differ.

The 8-, 24-, and 48-point collinear tiers span 6x, preserve coordinate uniqueness, and exercise repeated equal-distance groups around many pivots. The protected source passed all 10 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 0.98x the reference runtime. A correct O(n^3) ordered-triple enumeration passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 48.93x.

The Approach now exactly matches the reviewed target by noting that its inner loop also visits the pivot, whose sole zero-distance entry cannot contribute because points are unique. It accurately derives the incremental 2c contribution, proves the final m(m - 1) group count, and states O(n^2) time and O(n) auxiliary space.

The hash-bound Reference was checked against the live public statement. It preserves distinct planar points, ordered boomerang semantics, all three exact examples in source order, the two explicit ordered tuples in the first explanation, and all five constraints. The fabricated legacy third example was replaced by the source's single-point example.
